predictions.selection_reason: configuration string with ${...} pattern -> direct substitution of environment variable value -> potential injection if value used unsafely
predictions.source_summary: Environment variables from context.env (defaults to process.env) via ${VARNAME} patterns in configuration strings
predictions.sink_summary: The interpolated values are stored in the final configuration object and can be used by application code. The ExecutionInterpreter (#{...}) can execute JavaScript code that may use these values.
predictions.guard_summary: No validation or sanitization of environment variable values before substitution. The substitution is direct string replacement without escaping.
predictions.risk_pattern: Environment variable values are directly substituted into configuration strings without validation, potentially enabling injection attacks when these values flow to code execution contexts or other sensitive operations.
predictions.context_summary: EnvVarInterpreter processes ${VAR} patterns in configuration strings by replacing them with environment variable values. These values can flow to ExecutionInterpreter which executes JavaScript code using vm.runInNewContext.
unresolved_facts: How the final configuration object is used by consuming applications
Whether environment variables are considered trusted or attacker-controlled in deployment scenarios
What security-sensitive operations the configuration values might influence
